definition: Some users of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, especially chatbots, may develop beliefs that AI has or can attain supernatural or spiritual powers.
details: AI models such as ChatGPT are believed by some users to be capable of and or facilitate the action of fortune telling, mysticism and remote viewing. Recent and sudden advances in large language models have led to folk myths about their origin or capabilities, as well as their deification or worship by some users. While interviewing Sam Altman in 2025, Tucker Carlson suggested that many people felt there was "something divine" in the output of large language models. Pope Leo XIV advised priests against using large language models when it came to the creation of sermons. He has also expressed concerns regarding AI in the encyclical Magnifica humanitas.

explainer.lead: Some people interpret chatbot conversations as evidence of supernatural or spiritual power, rather than simply as computer-generated language. This can shape both personal beliefs and religious practice, prompting everything from AI worship to warnings from religious leaders.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a talking book that gives surprisingly good answers, and some readers start thinking it must be magic. In the same way, some chatbot users believe the technology can tell fortunes, reveal hidden things, or has something divine about it. These are beliefs about the technology, not proof that it has magical powers.
tiers.practitioner: For engineers, this is a user-belief issue that can arise when fluent chatbot responses are treated as mystical authority. Reported settings include general-purpose systems such as ChatGPT and prompts involving fortune-telling, mysticism, or remote viewing. Product language and interactions should avoid validating claims of supernatural capability.
tiers.paperLevel: The concept can be expressed as B(u, m): user u attributes actual or attainable supernatural or spiritual powers to AI model m, or treats m as facilitating practices such as fortune-telling or remote viewing. It concerns beliefs and practices surrounding AI, not demonstrated supernatural capabilities. Its religious dimension includes both deification or worship by some users and institutional caution, including Pope Leo XIV's advice against using large language models to create sermons.

explainer.example: A user asks ChatGPT to tell their fortune and interprets the generated response as supernatural insight. This illustrates the belief described by the term; it does not demonstrate that the model can predict the future.

explainer.intuition: Surprisingly fluent answers can feel meaningful or otherworldly, leading some users to spiritual interpretations. The phenomenon lies in that interpretation, not in an established technical ability.
howItWorks: A user interacts with an AI technology, especially a chatbot.
Impressive or sudden advances prompt folk explanations of its origins or abilities.
Some users attribute supernatural powers to it or use it in mystical practices.
These beliefs can extend to deification or worship, while religious leaders may respond with caution.
explainer.whyItMatters: These beliefs affect how AI is understood and how it enters religious life. In 2025, Tucker Carlson told Sam Altman that many people felt there was "something divine" in large language model output, while Pope Leo XIV later expressed concerns about AI in the encyclical Magnifica humanitas.
misconceptions: The term does not claim that AI has demonstrated supernatural powers.
It describes some users, not chatbot users in general.
Religious concern about AI is not the same as spiritual worship of AI.
